deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the neighbouring pages. k is a commutative ring and Ab_k is the category of k-modules. P is a small k-linear category. P^& = Hom_k(P^o, Ab_k) is the category of k-linear presheaves (right P-modules). For a k-additive category M, P^&_M = Hom_k(P^o, M) is the category of M-valued k-linear presheaves. Throughout, an object a of P is identified with its representable presheaf.

(1) External tensor. For L in P^& and x in M, Grothendieck sets L ⊗_k x = (a ↦ L(a) ⊗_k x), an object of P^&_M. This needs M to admit tensors U ⊗_k x by k-modules, e.g. M cocomplete.

(2) Example M = Q^&, Q another small k-linear category. Then P^&_M ≅ (P ⊗_k Q)^&, which is the category of k-bilinear functors P^o × Q^o → Ab_k. The pairing (*) becomes the external tensor product of presheaves, F ⊗ G ↦ ((a,b) ↦ F(a) ⊗_k G(b)). Grothendieck first wrote that this is fully faithful, then struck it out. He notes instead that the objects a ⊗ b generate P^&_M.

(3) Formula. * denotes the functor tensor product (coend) P^& × P^{o&} → Ab_k, extended to M-valued F. For L in P^& and L' in P^{o&}:
(L ⊗_k x) * L' ≅ (L * L') ⊗_k x.
The proof reduces to representables L = a, L' = b: both sides are canonically Hom(b,a) ⊗_k x. The general case follows because both sides are right exact and commute with sums in each variable.

(4) Adjunction. For F in P^&_M define Hom(x,F) in P^& by a ↦ Hom_M(x, F(a)). Then
Hom_{P^&_M}(L ⊗ x, F) ≅ Hom_M(x, Hom_k(L,F)) ≅ Hom_{P^&}(L, Hom(x,F)).
On a representable L = a, both last terms give Hom_M(x, F(a)) (Yoneda).

(5) Corollary. If L is projective in P^& and x is projective in M, then L ⊗ x is projective in P^&_M. Indeed Hom(L ⊗ x, -) is the composite of two exact functors when epimorphisms are objectwise, e.g. M abelian.

(6) Question. If M is k-additive, cocomplete and has enough projectives, does P^&_M have enough projectives, so that derived functors Tor_i(L,F) of F * L exist? The next page answers this: every F is a quotient of ⊕_a a ⊗ x_a with x_a projective mapping onto F(a). It then builds the derived tensor F ⊛^L L by projective resolutions, under flatness hypotheses on N.

Purpose. This is part of a programme ('Abelianization') of developing k-linear presheaf categories with coefficients in an additive category M. The aim is a derived functor tensor product P^&_M × P^{o&} → M, presumably as groundwork for abelianizing homotopy-type or stack constructions.
errors: The claim that P^& ⊗_k Q^& → (P⊗_k Q)^& is fully faithful was struck out, and rightly so. It is false in general: only the generation statement holds.

The middle term Hom_M(x, Hom_k(L,F)) presupposes cotensors (ends ∫_a F(a)^{L(a)}) in M, i.e. that M has limits. This is not stated at that point; the bottom line's 'stable par lim' is ambiguous between limits and colimits.
The projectivity corollary tacitly assumes that epimorphisms in P^&_M are objectwise, e.g. M abelian.

The Question is easily answered affirmatively, as done on the next page. The genuinely nontrivial point is the flatness condition needed for the derived tensor to be balanced, which is handled on page 12.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine homological algebra of modules over k-linear categories with coefficients in an additive category. It is careful and correct, with Grothendieck's characteristic notation (P^&, *_k), but the results are standard (Mitchell, Kelly, Keller). Nothing here seems absent from the literature.

Left margin bottom: 'si L = a ∈ P on trouve Hom_M(x, F(a)) pour les 2 derniers membres'.
